sections.editorialFinding: The opening needs the genealogical interval since Adam, Noah's identity, corruption of the earth, the command to make an ark, the covenant and Noah's obedience. The existing twelve-verse held reading is more faithful than the seven-verse option: it retains the explicitly named sons, the detail of corruption, the animals, the provisions and compliance. Architectural measurements Genesis 6:15–16 can remain an honestly disclosed omission.
essentialVerseRoles: God orders the construction of the ark
living creatures, provisions and faithful obedience
sections.theologyRisk: Do not present shortened fragments as a complete Flood account or represent a guessed chronology from the generations of Adam.

sections.editorialFinding: Exodus 11:4–8 foretells the firstborn judgment, Exodus 12:27–28 closes the Passover instructions, and Exodus 12:29–30 describes their fulfilment and the great cry in Egypt before the release order. Verse 29 gives the cause, verse 30 gives Pharaoh's reaction; the passage is only two verses and has not been included in the obligatory source selection.
essentialVerseRoles: Pharaoh's release and Israel's departure already selected
sections.theologyRisk: Do not collapse solemn Passover judgments to an invented narrator's sentence or treat divine forewarning as the actual occurrence.

sections.editorialFinding: Burial alone repairs the sepulchre antecedent. Yet John 19:31–37 is not redundant: it attests Christ's death, the unbroken bones, the piercing, blood and water, the explicit eyewitness testimony and two fulfilment quotations. At 161 Douay words, retaining this separate witness adds approximately 1 minute 14 seconds at 130 wpm over burial-only, a small economy gain compared with its unique witness content. The strongest integrity trial should compare all John 19:31–42 consecutively (303 Douay words total), without merging the trial ownership or approving either section.

piercing of His side and immediate blood and water

new sepulchre and placing the body
Magdalene's arrival and report at the sepulchre

sections.theologyRisk: A minimal burial-only repair misses distinct Johannine testimony in verses 31–37. Do not imply these seven original Scripture verses are expendable, and do not invent sacramental commentary inside the chronological narrative.

sections.editorialFinding: Paul's public mission between the Jerusalem Council and his Rome lodging has several intervening journeys. The source-labeled editorial transition can cite the arrest, appeal and journey. Exact Acts 28:16 locates the arrival and custody; 17–22 provides the Roman Jewish leaders, Paul's testimony and their request for a later hearing. Acts 28:23's appointed date is now intelligible. The reader must still explicitly mark the Acts 15→28 historical elision.

sections.theologyRisk: The seven-verse arrival/audience source is a local causal repair only. It cannot substitute a story of all of Acts 16–27 or justify synthesizing Paul's journey.

sections.editorialFinding: This is not a missing event in apostolic chronology. Historical Acts ends with Paul's Rome preaching; John's Apocalypse is a different canonical work, speaker and literary genre. A visibly non-Scripture heading is required even if no source verse is added. The held Revelation 4:1–2 provides a throne/voice antecedent for Revelation 5:1; optional Revelation 1:9–11 identifies John and Patmos but must be marked as non-contiguous to Revelation 4.

sections.theologyRisk: Do not turn the vision into a dated historical event, invent an encounter of Paul and John, or obscure major unselected intervening Revelation chapters.
